video_title: Draymond Green's Keys to Thunder vs Spurs Game 7 & Thoughts on Flopping!

quotes.speaker: Draymond Green
quotes.summary_phrase: Draymond Green defends Shai Gilgeous-Alexander against criticism of his playstyle
quotes.excerpt: None of the conversation has been about the elite level of play that Shai Gilgeous-Alexander brings.
quotes.quote: This series has been interesting because the storylines have been about Shai Gilgeous-Alexander flopping too much, or the referees calling too many fouls for Shai, or Shai falling too much. What has not been appreciated is the elite level of play that Shai Gilgeous-Alexander brings to the court. The elite level of Stephen Curry-like play that Victor Wembanyama brings to the floor, where you are watching the game and at any moment you can miss one of the most insane things that you have ever seen a player do, a la Stephen Curry, when you are watching Victor Wembanyama. It is ironic that none of the conversation has been about that, or the play of Dylan Harper, who is a rookie and just keeps finding a way, or the elite level defense of Stefan Castle. Stefan Castle's turned the ball over too much to two games in a row of one turnover. Why are we not talking about these things? Because sports media sucks.

quotes.speaker: Draymond Green
quotes.summary_phrase: Draymond Green addresses criticism of Shai Gilgeous-Alexander's free throw shooting
quotes.excerpt: You have reached a new level of greatness, my man. Congratulations, your hard work has paid off.
quotes.quote: Everyone is complaining about Shai Gilgeous-Alexander getting too many free throw calls. Going into Game 6, Shai had shot five more free throws on the series than Victor Wembanyama. But the whole complaint is Shai is getting too many foul calls. I do not understand it. Shai, what I will say is, you have reached a new level of greatness, my man. Congratulations, your hard work has paid off. You have reached a new level of greatness because you have sports media heads coming out and talking about what they do not like about your greatness. Imagine that. You have people coming out talking about what they do not like about your greatness. That is incredible.

quotes.speaker: Draymond Green
quotes.summary_phrase: Draymond Green analyzes the impact of injuries on the Thunder's rotation
quotes.excerpt: When you take your secondary ball handler like Jalen Williams off the floor against a great team.
quotes.quote: When you take your secondary ball handler like Jalen Williams off the floor against a great team, yes, they have been able to do it all regular season, yes, they have been able to do it through the playoffs, but now they are playing the second-best team in the Western Conference. It catches up to them at times. Then you take your third best ball handler, AJ Mitchell, off the floor, it catches up to you. So now all of a sudden Jared McCain has to handle a little bit more. I do not know that he is best suited handling and creating for himself. He gets to it at times, but I do not know that he is best suited, especially not on the road. At home, a little bit more comfortable. They are going to bump you a little bit less because you get the home whistle. That is just how things go. You get the home whistle, you are going to get a little better whistle at home.

quotes.speaker: Draymond Green
quotes.summary_phrase: Draymond Green discusses De'Aaron Fox's performance and injury status
quotes.excerpt: De'Aaron Fox missed the first couple games, hasn't quite been himself, struggling a bit.
quotes.quote: De'Aaron Fox missed the first couple games, has not quite been himself, struggling a bit. You wonder if that is due to the injury. I have seen Fox in the playoffs, Fox is not one to go hide and he is not one that struggles with pressure or big moments. Fox is not that guy. Now, this is the biggest moment of his career, furthest he has ever gone, of course, but Fox is not that guy. So he is a little banged up as well. It has kind of been a war of attrition. You hate that it turns into that, but it happens in series where you get games every other day.

quotes.speaker: Draymond Green
quotes.summary_phrase: Draymond Green on the importance of rotation decisions for Game 7
quotes.excerpt: If Jared got it, if Jared ain't got it, you kind of got to go away.
quotes.quote: You have to make a decision. If Jared got it, if Jared ain't got it, you kind of got to go away. Kind of got to trust the guys that have been doing it because Jared ain't played much all year, let alone throughout these playoffs. Game 7, but Jared is a champion and I believe, although he has not played, he is one of those guys, he can muster up something in a Game 7. He has been there. That matters when you know how to do it, right? So, but they kind of need to figure that out fast. I do not think this is like, oh man, we are going into the second half seeing if he find it in the second half. Not saying he cannot, but I just do not know if that is what they want to go with.
